name: Alpheius of Mitylene
bio: Alpheius of Mitylene is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors dates the poet to 1st century AD. Paton's index lists the poet among the writers of the Wreath of Philippus, the Garland compiled in the first century AD.
This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the second volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book VII: 237).

poems.title: Book VII, 237
poems.author: Alpheius of Mitylene
poems.text: Carve on my tomb the mountains and the sea, and midmost of both the sun as witness; yea, and the deep currents of the ever-flowing rivers, whose streams sufficed not for Xerxes’ host of the thousand ships. Carve Salamis too, here where the Magnesian people proclaim the tomb of dead Themistocles.
